headers._comment: Photographs are slug-named rather than content-hashed, so this carries the same hazard the favicons hit: re-cropping a photo under an existing slug would be invisible to anyone who had already loaded it. Kept immutable because these are the largest assets on the site and revalidating ~100 of them costs real time on a mobile connection. If a photograph is ever re-cropped, change its slug rather than its bytes.
Self-hosted fonts. Stable names, but the bytes for a given name never change - a new weight or subset is a new filename - so immutable is safe here.

Icons, the social card and the manifest are UNVERSIONED names whose CONTENT changes in place. A blanket immutable rule for png/jpg/ico used to catch them, which told every browser never to revalidate for a year - so a favicon change never reached anyone who had already loaded the old one. Immutable is only ever correct for content-hashed URLs. These revalidate against their ETag, which is a 304 and costs nothing when unchanged. Written as separate literal sources rather than one alternation: Vercel parses `source` with path-to-regexp, where nested groups do not mean what they mean in a raw regex.
